newsitem.title: FRANCE: Chirac hails budget as serious on spending, Europe.
newsitem.headline: Chirac hails budget as serious on spending, Europe.

text.p: President Jacques Chirac said the 1997 budget approved by the cabinet on Wednesday was in line with France's European commitments and economic harmonisation with Germany, government spokesman Alain Lamassoure said.

"He welcomed the drive in the budget proposals to get back to reality," Lamassoure said. "For the first time in the history of the Fifth Republic there has been a genuine attempt to halt the rise in public spending," he quoted Chirac as saying.
"This is a serious fiscal reform, the budget is in line with our European commitments and Franco-German policy, Chirac added, according to Lamassoure.
For Jacques Chirac, there were "two things that should be avoided like the plague -- administrative humdrum and the imagination of the dogmatic", Lamassoure said.

Chirac, drawing on an anecdote from his student days at the beginning of the Fifth Republic, alluded to General de Gaulle saying, "you can't spend more than you earn" and "reform must be carried out to spend more efficiently".
This axiom applied perfectly to the current situation, Lamassoure quoted Chirac as saying.
